title: F2A-ObjectNav: An Adaptive Agentic Architecture for Object-Goal Navigation

problem.summary: Object-goal navigation requires an embodied agent to explore an unfamiliar environment, identify a target object, navigate toward candidate instances, and reliably determine whether the observed object satisfies the mission goal.
statements: Object-goal navigation requires an embodied agent to explore an unfamiliar environment, identify a target object, navigate toward candidate instances, and reliably determine whether the observed object satisfies the mission goal.
This work investigates this problem through a two-stage development process.
In Stage I, a fixed modular framework is used to examine combinations of exploration, object detection, and target validation methods.

background.summary: A configuration that is effective during straightforward search may become less suitable after repeated exploration or ambiguous detections, whereas continuously invoking computationally expensive semantic reasoning may be unnecessary when conventional perception and navigation are sufficient.

solution.summary: Object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) requires an embodied agent to locate a target object in an unfamiliar environment without being given its position in advance [1].
solution.approach: Object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) requires an embodied agent to locate a target object in an unfamiliar environment without being given its position in advance [1].
components: Unlike point-goal navigation, where the destination is specified geometrically, ObjectNav requires the agent to infer where the target may be located, explore the environment, identify potential instances, navigate toward them, and determine whether an observed candidate satisfies the intended goal.
Successful execution therefore depends on the coordinated operation of perception, exploration, navigation, and target verification over an extended sequence of decisions [1, 2].
This coordination remains challenging because the information available to the agent is partial and changes throughout the mission.

F2A-ObjectNav follows a different design principle: mission-level coordination remains rule-based, while language and multimodal models are restricted to specialized functions such as goal interpretation, target validation, and conditional semantic guidance.
